title: What If You Nuked a Burning Gas Well? The Soviets Did. It Took 23 Seconds

scenes.text: What if you set off a nuclear bomb to put out a fire? In 1966, it worked.
In December 1963, a gas well in Uzbekistan blew out and burned for nearly three years.
It wasted twelve million cubic meters of gas every single day. Nothing engineers tried could stop it.
So they drilled a slanted shaft and lowered a thirty-kiloton nuclear device 1,500 meters down, beside the well.
On September 30th, 1966, it went off. The shock squeezed the rock shut around the pipe.
Twenty-three seconds later the flame was out. No radiation above normal was measured at the surface, and the Soviets used the trick four more times.

description:
What if you used a nuclear bomb to put out a fire? On 30 September 1966 the Soviet Union did exactly that at the Urtabulak gas field in Uzbekistan.
Well No. 11 had blown out on 1 December 1963 and burned for almost three years, losing about 12 million cubic meters of gas a day. Engineers drilled an inclined shaft and set off a 30-kiloton device about 1,500 meters down, within a few dozen meters of the well, so that the shock would shift the rock and pinch the shaft closed. The fire went out 23 seconds later, with radiation at the surface reported within normal limits. The method was used on four more wells; the last attempt, in 1981, failed.
